cohort: 2241 deliveries (381 cases with arterial cord blood pH at birth ≤7.15 and 1860 controls with pH ≥7.25) from a database of 8383 full datasets of mothers over 18 years old who had vaginal or cesarean non-twin, non-breech deliveries at term (>37 weeks of amenorrhea)
finding: In addition to clinical factors like nulliparity, male fetus, and gestational age, automated analysis of fetal heart rate (FHR) identified baseline range, FHR signal instability, and late deceleration area as significant predictors of umbilical cord acidosis.
